title: Transcranial alternating current stimulation as psychiatric intervention: A meta-analytic primer
title_zh: 经颅交替电流刺激作为精神干预：元分析综述导引
abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) is an emerging neuromodulation approach targeting neural oscillations. Although mechanistic studies support its neurophysiological effects, clinical evidence across psychiatric symptoms remains limited. This transdiagnostic meta-analysis provides a quantitative assessment of tACS effects across psychiatric symptom domains and identifies areas of clinical promise. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized sham-controlled trials assessing tACS in adults with psychiatric conditions was conducted. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and CENTRAL were searched until August 2026. Standardized mean differences (Hedges' g) were calculated using random-effects models, with exploratory analyses investigating clinical and methodological moderators. RESULTS: Eighteen studies (19 datasets; 1045 participants) were included. Compared with sham stimulation, tACS showed a moderate overall effect (SMD = -0.41, 95% CI [-0.60, -0.2], I2 = 72%). The strongest significant findings were observed for depressive symptoms (n = 10; SMD = -0.44, 95% CI -0.76 to -0.01) and anxiety symptoms (n = 4; SMD = -0.64, 95% CI -1.12 to -0.17, I2 = 62%). Significant improvements were also observed for obsessive-compulsive symptoms, inattention, and post-traumatic stress symptoms, although based on limited evidence. Exploratory analyses identified preliminary patterns across stimulation frequencies and symptom domains, including significant effects of gamma-frequency stimulation on depressive symptoms. CONCLUSION: This transdiagnostic meta-analysis identifies early therapeutic signals of tACS across psychiatric symptoms, with the most consistent evidence observed for depressive symptoms. Frequency-specific effects may influence clinical outcomes and warrant further investigation to optimize stimulation parameters.
abstract_zh: 背景：经颅交替电流刺激（tACS）是一种针对神经振荡的新兴神经调控方法。尽管机制研究支持其神经生理效应，但其在精神症状方面的临床证据仍然有限。本跨诊断元分析对tACS在精神疾病患者中的症状领域进行了定量评估，并确定了临床前景领域。方法：在成人精神疾病患者中进行的经颅交替电流刺激随机安慰剂对照试验的系统评估和元分析。检索了MEDLINE/PubMed、Embase、Scopus和CENTRAL，检索截止至2026年8月。使用随机效应模型计算标准化均值差（Hedges' g），并进行探索性分析研究临床和方法学调节因子。结果：共纳入18项研究（19个数据集；1045名参与者）。与安慰剂刺激相比，tACS表现出中等整体效应（SMD = -0.41，95% CI [-0.60, -0.2]，I2 = 72%）。观察到最显著的结果是针对抑郁症状（n = 10；SMD = -0.44，95% CI -0.76 to -0.01）和焦虑症状（n = 4；SMD = -0.64，95% CI -1.12 to -0.17，I2 = 62%）。对于强迫症状、注意力不集中和创伤后应激症状也观察到了显著改善，尽管证据有限。探索性分析确定了频率与症状领域之间的初步模式，包括γ频率刺激对抑郁症状的显著效应。结论：本跨诊断元分析确定了tACS在精神症状方面的早期治疗信号，最一致的证据集中在抑郁症状上。频率特异性效应可能影响临床结果，需要进一步研究以优化刺激参数。
